title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Wall St pared earlier losses but still fell Monday — S&P 500 -1%, Nasdaq -0.7%, Dow -1.6% (-848pts) — as AI-valuation jitters persisted; the Nasdaq had been down as much as 2% intraday.

Markets: The 10-year Treasury yield eased to 5.105% (from 5.122%) after soft October retail sales; Anthropic's IPO reportedly priced above its $70-78 range on strong demand, with ANT shares expected to begin trading on Nasdaq Nov. 19.

Companies: Nvidia reported solid Q3 earnings after the bell, though shares still slipped 0.5% on the day; separately, WSJ reports the SEC is probing Nvidia amid Jensen Huang's abrupt departure as CEO.

Companies: Huang said he'd be 'honored' to return as Nvidia CEO if asked, but the board isn't considering it; UBS estimates up to $50B could exit the AI ecosystem if Nvidia pulls back its vendor financing.

Companies: Home Depot's CEO Ted Decker is stepping down after medical leave (shares -2.5%) even as the retailer raised full-year guidance; Disney targets $3B in annual cost cuts by FY2029 under new CEO Josh D'Amaro (shares -1.5%).

Macro/Policy: October retail sales grew just 0.2% (vs. 0.8% in Sept.), suggesting the tax-cut spending boost is fading; FOMC minutes are due Wednesday, with Fed's Barr and Kashkari speaking and Oct. housing starts/pending home sales ahead.

Macro/Policy: California's AG sued OpenAI over agent-driven cyberattacks, rejecting the idea that AI firms can 'pass off blame to machines' — part of a broader regulatory tightening around AI providers.
